content.title: 'Malcolm in the Middle' cast is back. Who's returning and who's new?
content.text: April 6, 2026Updated April 13, 2026, 12:19 a.m. ETIt may be 20 years after we left Malcolm as an aggrieved teen who's exasperated by his family, but life is still unfair for him in the "Malcolm in the Middle" revival.In the four-episode "Malcolm in the Middle: Life’s Still Unfair" (streaming on Hulu and Hulu on Disney+ April 10), a now-adult Malcolm (Frankie Muniz) sees his carefully curated life away from his dysfunctional family – parents Hal (Bryan Cranston) and Lois (Jane Kaczmarek) along with five siblings – implode. For the first time his girlfriend Tristan (Kiana Madeira) and daughter Leah (Keeley Karsten) are exposed to his chaotic family.The catalyst for this cataclysmic event? Lois and Hal's 40th anniversary party.Plenty of original cast members from the 2000-2006 Fox show are returning for the one-off revival, with the exception of two changes to the family's cast. And, as the series unfolds, some special cameos are in store for longtime fans.For those who need a refresher on who's who – and casual fans who might be wondering if Malcolm always had that many siblings – here's a breakdown on who's returning and who's been recast in the "Malcolm" revival.Frankie Muniz plays MalcolmWith three younger siblings, Malcolm may no longer necessarily be "in the middle." But he'll always be Frankie Muniz.Muniz returns as the smart-alecky, exasperated teen who's always either fighting with his siblings or ganging up on his parents – just 20 years older. And Malcolm's life is "fantastic." His secret? Staying "completely away from my family."Bryan Cranston returns as dad HalHal, the well-meaning, loving but often bumbling patriarch, is back with Bryan Cranston once again playing him.But Hal is apparently in a spiral following Malcolm's betrayal in the revival; in the trailer, he asks his newfound granddaughter, "What do you want to do when you grow up? Crush your father's soul and make him question his own identity?"Jane Kaczmarek reprises role of mom LoisWith Jane Kaczmarek reprising her role as the stressed-out family disciplinarian Lois, the matriarch is dead set on celebrating her 40th wedding anniversary.Even after all these decades, her love clearly knows no bounds, as she is seen shaving her husband's back and, well, some more intimate areas, at the opening of the four-part show's trailer.Christopher Masterson is back as FrancisNo matter how many kids his parents might bring into the family, Francis – again played by Christopher Masterson – will always be the rebellious firstborn son who dropped out of military school. And he's still with his wife, Piama (Emy Coligado), whom he met during his jaunt to Alaska.Justin Berfield is back as ReeseJustin Berfield's Reese is back, albeit without his signature spiky hairdo that was all the rage in the 2000s.He's as conniving as ever, telling his dad in the trailer: "I think we all knew Malcolm would eventually betray us." The second eldest son later tells a sleeping Hal, "By comparison, Reese looks pretty good."Why Erik Per Sullivan didn't return as DeweyAt the beginning of the "Life's Still Unfair" trailer, a disgusted Dewey is video chatting with his parents as Lois thoroughly shaves Hal down. But Dewey is now played by Caleb Ellsworth-Clark, rather than the quietly hilarious Erik Per Sullivan.The show's creator, Linwood Boomer, told USA TODAY that he wasn't able to reel Sullivan back in despite his best efforts; the former actor is now working toward his master's degree at Harvard University."Eric Sullivan hasn't been an actor for decades. I asked him to repeat [Dewey]. We still talk all the time. I love him, and he didn't want to be an actor anymore," Boomer says. "He didn't like [acting] 10 years ago, and he sure doesn't now. I had to respect that."Boomer added that Sullivan encouraged him to "please just recast it. It's fine." The team found Ellsworth-Clark.The actor "really looks like Eric. He also really inhabits Dewey in a way that seems very believable," Boomer says. "It really felt like this is how Dewey would be 20 years later."Baby Jamie is recast with Anthony TimpanoLest you forget the fourth child, Lois gave birth to her and Hal's youngest son, Jamie, with the help of their eldest, Francis, at the end of Season 4.Jamie was played by twins James and Lukas Rodriguez from 2004 to 2006. But in the "Malcolm" revival – with Jamie briefly seen in the anniversary party scene and also in uniform with a "U.S. Coast Guard" sign behind him in a gallery-view Zoom call – he is portrayed by Anthony Timpano, per IMDb.Vaughan Murrae is newest sibling KellyIn the 20 years since we left Lois and Hal, they've apparently welcomed their sixth child, Kelly. The newcomer to the cast is played by Vaughan Murrae, who uses they and them pronouns.Keeley Karsten is Malcolm's daughter, LeahJoining a zany family that she didn't even know she had is Leah, Malcolm's high school-aged daughter. She's played by Keeley Karsten.Contributing: Bryan Alexander, USA TODAY
